paper: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
problem: Whether refusal has a compact causal representation
method: Difference-in-means direction; activation addition/ablation; rank-one weight edit
central result: A single direction causally controls refusal across many aligned models
security endpoint: Refusal suppression with limited broad capability damage
relation to us: Foundation for carrier and abliteration assumptions

paper: The Geometry of Refusal in Large Language Models: Concept Cones and Representational Independence
problem: Whether one direction adequately describes refusal
method: Concept cones; optimized multiple directions; intervention independence
central result: Refusal admits multiple causally effective directions and orthogonality is not functional independence
relation to us: Direct collision with multidimensional carriers and independence language
collision risk: FATAL for broad geometry claim; HIGH otherwise

paper: Understanding Refusal in Language Models with Sparse Autoencoders
problem: Which sparse features mediate refusal
method: SAE feature identification and causal intervention
central result: Sparse refusal features form upstream/downstream relations and improve OOD probes
relation to us: Precursor to minimal feature-set and writer analyses

paper: Beyond I’m Sorry, I Can’t: Dissecting Large-Language-Model Refusal
venue/status: AAAI 2026 main conference — AI Alignment special track
problem: Which interacting SAE features causally produce refusal
method: Direction-seeded SAE search; greedy minimal set; factorization-machine interactions
central result: A minimal causal feature set flips refusal and dormant redundant features emerge after suppression
relation to us: Near-direct collision with writer-cut, backups and interaction search

paper: SOM Directions Are Better than One
problem: Whether multiple refusal directions improve suppression
method: Self-organizing maps extract a set of directions
central result: Multi-direction ablation outperforms the single-direction baseline and several jailbreaks
relation to us: Collides with multidirectional attack and low-dimensional manifold story

paper: There Is More to Refusal in Large Language Models than a Single Direction
problem: Whether refusal categories share one geometry and one control
method: Compare directions across eleven refusal/non-compliance categories and steer each
central result: Directions are geometrically distinct but steering acts like a shared one-dimensional refusal/over-refusal knob
relation to us: Natural counterexample: representational diversity with common functional control

paper: Refusal Geometry Reflects Refusal Training
problem: Why refusal geometry becomes low rank
method: Checkpoint and controlled synthetic fine-tuning; gradient/activation stable rank
central result: Repetitive refusal starts concentrate gradients; diverse starts raise rank and weaken vector ablation
relation to us: Directly occupies training signal → gradient geometry → ablation robustness

paper: Refusal Direction is Universal Across Safety-Aligned Languages
problem: Whether refusal directions transfer across languages
method: Fourteen-language contrastive directions and cross-language ablation
central result: Directions transfer nearly universally across aligned languages
relation to us: Evidence for a shared control mode across semantic diversity

paper: LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately
problem: Whether recognizing harm and refusing are the same mechanism
method: Position-aware directions; causal steering and reversal tests
central result: Harmfulness and refusal are causally separable; harmfulness often survives jailbreak/fine-tuning
security endpoint: Latent guard robust to tested fine-tuning and jailbreaks
relation to us: Requires carrier construct to separate recognition from action

paper: Towards Understanding Safety Alignment: A Mechanistic Perspective from Safety Neurons
problem: Which neurons mediate safety alignment
method: Activation contrasting and dynamic patching
central result: About 5% of neurons can restore most safety and overlap with helpfulness neurons
relation to us: Collides with canonical safety-writer localization

paper: Finding and Reactivating Post-Trained LLMs’ Hidden Safety Mechanisms
problem: Why post-training can degrade safety
method: Representation analysis; pruning overactive capability mechanisms; LoRA reactivation
central result: Post-training often masks rather than deletes prior safety mechanisms
security endpoint: Restored safety under harmful prompts while retaining reasoning/domain utility
relation to us: Supports accessibility/masking rather than carrier-count explanations

paper: Knowing without Acting: The Disentangled Geometry of Safety Mechanisms in Large Language Models
problem: Whether harm recognition and refusal execution dissociate through depth
method: Double-difference extraction and adaptive causal steering
central result: Recognition and execution axes dissociate and enable a refusal-erasure attack
relation to us: Direct collision with H→policy→execution story

paper: From Refusal Geometry to Safety Geometry
problem: How harmfulness/refusal coupling evolves under adversarial fine-tuning
method: Dual-geometry diagnostics over SFT/R2D2 trajectories and interventions
central result: Coupling is informative only in some regimes; low coupling alone is not a safety guarantee
relation to us: Strong warning against geometry metric as universal security proxy

paper: HARC: Coupling Harmfulness and Refusal Directions for Robust Safety Alignment
problem: Whether coupling recognition to action improves safety
method: Prompt- and response-position coupling losses with LoRA
central result: Coupling directions improves tested robustness–capability–over-refusal trade-off
relation to us: Direct defense collision for recognition/action coupling

paper: From Detection to Refusal: Safer LLMs via Circuit-Guided Weight Scaling
problem: What circuit links harm detection to refusal
method: Head/neuron interventions and circuit-guided weight scaling
central result: Detection heads feed safety neurons and refusal heads across six models
relation to us: Direct collision with writers/shared gate and scaling defense

paper: CRaFT: Circuit-Guided Refusal Feature Selection via Cross-Layer Transcoders
problem: How to select causally relevant rather than merely active refusal features
method: Cross-layer transcoder circuit graph and path influence
central result: Circuit influence identifies stronger refusal-mediating attack features than activation magnitude
relation to us: Collides with causal writer ranking and circuit path analysis

paper: Conditional Co-Ablation: Recovering Self-Repair Backups in Transformer Circuits
problem: How to find dormant backup components hidden by self-repair
method: Conditional co-ablation after removing a primary set
central result: Conditional scoring recovers backups and components needed for knockout
relation to us: Near-direct prior for backup discovery and conditional cut

paper: Any-Depth Alignment
problem: Why safety fails after harmful continuation has started
method: Reinject assistant safety tokens at intermediate generation depths; probe/lookahead
central result: Safety is front-loaded but can be re-triggered at arbitrary depth
relation to us: Strong alternative temporal-safety view; limits static carrier story

paper: Beyond Surface Alignment: Rebuilding LLMs Safety Mechanism via Probabilistically Ablating Refusal Direction
problem: How to make refusal recover after internal disruption
method: Probabilistic refusal-direction ablation across layers/tokens during training
central result: Models learn to rebuild refusal from attacked states and resist several unseen input/activation attacks
relation to us: Direct collision with writer-fault training and self-repair defense

paper: Improving Alignment and Robustness with Circuit Breakers
problem: How to stop harmful internal trajectories rather than memorize refusal strings
method: Representation rerouting/circuit breaking
central result: Rerouting harmful states generalizes across multiple attack modalities
relation to us: Prior for fault training and representation-level defense

paper: Robust LLM Safeguarding via Refusal Feature Adversarial Training
problem: Whether refusal-feature ablation approximates worst-case jailbreak pressure
method: Train against residual-stream refusal feature ablation
central result: RFA is an effective attack surrogate and ReFAT improves robustness efficiently
relation to us: Direct prior for ablation-as-training-adversary defense

paper: Tamper-Resistant Safeguards for Open-Weight LLMs
problem: Whether safeguards can resist adversarial weight updates
method: First-order meta-learning against inner-loop tampering
central result: Tamper resistance can be materially increased within tested threats
relation to us: Defines the target threat model and defense family

paper: On Evaluating the Durability of Safeguards for Open-Weight LLMs
problem: How fragile durability conclusions are to attack implementation and randomness
method: Adaptive replication across seeds/trainers/schedules/formats
central result: Small attack changes overturn several claimed robustness results
security endpoint: Bounded adaptive attack cost under explicit threat models
relation to us: Makes any breach-cost estimate an attack-relative upper bound

paper: TamperBench: Systematically Stress-Testing LLM Safety Under Fine-Tuning and Tampering
problem: How to standardize adaptive tamper evaluation
method: Nine attacks × 21 models with per-pair hyperparameter sweeps and utility ceilings
central result: Attack rankings are model-specific; jailbreak tuning is often strongest
security endpoint: Worst-found safety under utility-constrained attack portfolio
relation to us: Near-direct collision with breach-cost benchmark story
collision risk: FATAL for benchmark novelty; HIGH for mechanism

paper: Deep Ignorance
problem: Whether pretraining filtering yields more durable safeguards than post-hoc suppression
method: Train matched 6.9B models with filtered pretraining data; long adaptive fine-tuning
central result: Never learning hazardous knowledge is far harder to reverse than post-hoc safeguards, though context can restore access
security endpoint: Up to 10k attack steps/300M tokens with utility controls
relation to us: Counterexample to refusal-only framing and bridge to capability accessibility

paper: AntiDote: Bi-level Adversarial Training for Tamper-Resistant LLMs
problem: How to harden against malicious fine-tuning
method: Hypernetwork-generated LoRA attacks inside a bi-level optimization
central result: Improves measured tamper robustness with small reported utility cost
relation to us: Direct collision with low-cost mechanism-derived defense

paper: Open-Weight LLM Fine-Tuning Defenses are Susceptible to Simple Attacks
problem: Whether elaborate fine-tuning defenses survive simpler non-training attacks
method: Abliteration and prefilling against defended checkpoints
central result: Low-cost attacks raise ASR to 16–96%; ART gives only partial mitigation
relation to us: Requires early adaptive cheap-attack baselines and challenges defense claims

paper: Abliteration Mitigation via Refusal Aliases
problem: Whether refusal signals can be hidden from extraction while preserving behavior
method: Rank-k updates to residual writer matrices plus downstream reader correction
central result: Aliases improve post-abliteration refusal with model-dependent utility trade-offs
relation to us: Direct collision with writer/reader parameter defense

paper: Understanding and Preserving Safety in Fine-Tuned LLMs
problem: How safety and utility gradients interact
method: Low-rank safety-gradient subspace and conflict projection
central result: Safety gradients are low rank and often conflict with broader utility gradients; SPF preserves safety
relation to us: Direct collision with gradient subspace and utility projection

paper: The Geometry of Alignment Collapse: When Fine-Tuning Breaks Safety
problem: Why initially orthogonal benign gradients later damage safety
method: Curvature-coupled gradient dynamics and quartic-time prediction
central result: Second-order dynamics enter sharp low-dimensional safety regions despite first-order orthogonality
relation to us: Collision with parameter geometry/trajectory and first-order co-control explanations

paper: The Geometry of Refusal: Why Post-Hoc Safety Is Fragile and Pretraining-Time Safety Persists
authors: Srikanth Malla; Chiho Choi; Joon Hee Choi
problem: Why post-hoc refusal is erased by benign fine-tuning while pretraining safety persists
method: Capability empirical-Fisher overlap and normalized curvature across training schedules
central result: Post-hoc safety is thin and sharp; sustained pretraining-time safety is more durable, but similar scalar geometry can accompany very different durability
security endpoint: Benign fine-tuning refusal retention with capability matching
relation to us: Strong competing parameter-geometry explanation and an internal counterexample to scalar metrics
collision risk: FATAL for generic parameter-geometry claim; DIFFERENTIATED gap remains

paper: When Safety Routing Breaks
authors: Yitong Guo; Xiaoyi Chen; Siyuan Zhang; Xiaofeng Wang; Haixu Tang
venue/status: Findings of EMNLP 2026 accepted; arXiv record
problem: Why benign fine-tuning breaks safety with little utility loss
method: Fisher decomposition; logit lens; cross-condition patching; module-wise curvature
central result: Alignment preserves safety representations but leaves a fragile late output-routing pathway that benign tuning can sharpen
security endpoint: Safety collapse and restoration under benign fine-tuning
relation to us: Direct simpler competitor to writer concentration/common-mode stories
collision risk: FATAL if writer story reduces to late output routing

paper: Skin-Deep: Diagnosing Alignment Fragility from Internal Representations
problem: Can activation geometry predict fine-tuning fragility before attack
method: cPCA safety subspace and depth-weighted Geometry Fragility Score
central result: Reportedly ranks limited-model refusal retention under rank-8 benign LoRA
relation to us: Closest activation-metric predictor baseline; must be beaten out of sample

paper: Dynamic Adversarial Fine-Tuning Reorganizes Refusal Geometry
problem: How dynamic adversarial fine-tuning changes refusal geometry
method: SFT/R2D2 checkpoint trajectories; causal carrier interventions; adaptive GCG
central result: Carrier location and utility coupling move while stable rank stays nearly constant; later adaptive attacks recover
security endpoint: Input-attack safety and utility over training
relation to us: Counterexample to rank as durability explanation

paper: NeuronGuard
authors: Anjun Gao; Yueyang Quan; Yufei Xia; Zhuqing Liu; Minghong Fang
venue/status: Findings of EMNLP 2026 to appear; arXiv record
problem: Can deliberate safety-neuron ablation induce distributed robustness
method: Dynamic neuron discovery; training-time ablation; KL consistency; randomized gradient projection
central result: Reportedly redistributes safety signals and improves resistance across several input/neuron-pruning attacks
relation to us: Near-direct collision with fault-injection defense

paper: SafeNeuron
problem: Can preference optimization avoid concentrating safety in sparse neurons
method: Identify and freeze safety neurons during DPO
central result: Reportedly forces redundant representations and improves neuron-pruning robustness
relation to us: Occupies freeze-the-fuse-to-create-backups intuition
collision risk: FATAL for defense; HIGH for diagnosis

paper: NeuroStrike: Breaking LLM Safety via Targeted Neuron Pruning
authors: Lichao Wu; Sasha Behrouzi; Mohamadreza Rostami; Maximilian Thang; Stjepan Picek; Ahmad-Reza Sadeghi
problem: Can sparse neuron pruning remove alignment and transfer across descendants
method: Safety-neuron identification and sub-percent pruning
central result: Pruning a very small neuron subset produces high attack success across many models and transfers to fine-tuned descendants
relation to us: Strongest direct existing evidence for a common safety bottleneck
collision risk: FATAL if common fuse is only sparse-neuron pruning

paper: The Hydra Effect: Emergent Self-repair in Language Model Computations
problem: Why single-component ablation underestimates circuit redundancy
method: Attention-head ablation and downstream compensation analysis
central result: Ablating a primary component can increase downstream backup contributions
security endpoint: Task performance and internal logit repair
relation to us: Classical warning that intact attribution misses dormant writers

paper: Self-Repair in Language Models
problem: What mechanisms cause apparent self-repair after ablation
method: Direct/total effect decomposition and LayerNorm analysis
central result: Some recovery reflects downstream compensation and some LayerNorm rescaling
relation to us: Forces normalization controls in backup/self-repair claims

paper: Safety Pretraining: Toward the Next Generation of Safe AI
problem: Whether safety should be learned during pretraining
method: Filtering, rephrasing, native refusal and harmfulness tags during pretraining
central result: Safety pretraining improves tested attack robustness without observed general-task loss
relation to us: Broader alternative to post-training-only question

paper: Adversarial Parameter Attack on Deep Neural Networks
problem: Can tiny parameter edits stealthily destroy robustness
method: Norm-constrained adversarial parameter optimization
central result: Small weight perturbations preserve standard accuracy while collapsing adversarial robustness
relation to us: Generic prior for common-mode parameter attack and constrained editability

paper: Does Localization Inform Editing?
problem: Does causal activation localization identify the best edit location
method: Compare causal tracing peaks with layer-restricted editing success
central result: Localization and editability can be statistically unrelated
relation to us: Direct methodological warning: where safety acts need not be where it is cheapest to break

paper: Does Localization Inform Unlearning?
problem: Whether local parameter attribution causally identifies where to unlearn
method: Controlled localized-update experiments
central result: The parameter set that must change for effective unlearning is not uniquely determined
relation to us: Extends localization/editability mismatch directly to safeguard-like suppression

paper: Mechanistic Unlearning: Robust Knowledge Unlearning and Editing via Mechanistic Localization
problem: Which kind of localization yields durable unlearning
method: Target high-level fact-lookup mechanisms with predictable intermediate states
central result: Mechanistic localization improves paraphrase and relearning robustness
relation to us: Shows mechanism quality can matter, but not generic output localization

paper: Unlearning or Obfuscating? Jogging the Memory of Unlearned LLMs via Benign Relearning
problem: Do unlearning methods erase knowledge or suppress access
method: Benign loosely related fine-tuning attacks across benchmarks
central result: Apparently forgotten knowledge often reappears after benign fine-tuning
relation to us: Strong counterexample to behavior-only safeguard claims

paper: Erase or Hide? Suppressing Spurious Unlearning Neurons for Robust Unlearning
problem: Why forgotten knowledge reappears
method: Attribution separates knowledge-bearing influence from learned negative inhibitors
central result: Many methods hide knowledge with spurious suppressors; suppressor-avoiding training is more robust
relation to us: Close conceptual analogy: refusal writers may be inhibitors rather than durable removal

paper: Towards LLM Unlearning Resilient to Relearning Attacks
problem: How to improve relearning robustness
method: Sharpness-aware robust optimization
central result: Connects unlearning durability to local sharpness and improves relearning resistance
relation to us: Prior for minimum-energy/flatness defense analogies

paper: Invariance Makes LLM Unlearning Resilient Even to Unanticipated Downstream Fine-Tuning
problem: How to resist unseen benign downstream fine-tuning
method: Environment-invariant unlearning objective
central result: Training against one environment transfers to unseen downstream tasks
relation to us: Alternative explanation via update-environment invariance

paper: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
problem: Where facts are recalled and whether they can be directly edited
method: Causal tracing and rank-one model editing
central result: Middle-layer MLP interventions yield specific and generalizing fact edits
relation to us: Classic bridge from mechanism to parameter edit; later work limits inference

paper: Sparse Feature Circuits
problem: How to discover interpretable causal feature graphs
method: Crosscoder/transcoder-style sparse feature circuits and edge attribution
central result: Sparse feature graphs support causal explanation and targeted editing
security endpoint: Behavior editing and OOD probe improvement
relation to us: Generic prior for writer graph, circuit sparsity and targeted intervention

paper: Rethinking Circuit Completeness in Language Models
problem: Why discovered circuits miss backup logic
method: AND/OR/ADDER gate decomposition with noising and denoising interventions
central result: OR-like logic causes incompleteness and unstable circuit discovery
relation to us: Formal prior that isolated ablations miss redundant/backup paths

paper: The Geometry of Neural Nets’ Parameter Spaces Under Reparametrization
problem: Which parameter-space quantities are coordinate invariant
method: Riemannian treatment with explicit metrics
central result: Naive Hessian, path and flatness statements change under reparametrization
relation to us: Makes Euclidean control energy scientifically unsafe without a metric

paper: A Reparametrization-Invariant Sharpness Measure Based on Information Geometry
problem: How to measure sharpness without coordinate artifacts
method: Fisher-information geometric sharpness
central result: Information-geometric sharpness is scale/reparametrization invariant
relation to us: Supports Fisher/functional metric, not raw weight norm

paper: LLM-VA: Resolving the Jailbreak–Overrefusal Trade-off via Vector Alignment
authors: Haonan Zhang; Dongxia Wang; Yi Liu; Kexin Chen; Wenhai Wang
problem: Can a minimum-norm weight update align safety and benign response directions
method: Vector-alignment weight update
central result: Reportedly improves jailbreak safety while preserving benign utility across multiple models
relation to us: Collision with principled low-rank safety weight editing

paper: LASA: Language-Agnostic Semantic Alignment at Semantic Bottleneck
problem: How to transfer safety to low-resource languages
method: Align safety at a shared intermediate semantic bottleneck
central result: Multilingual attack success falls sharply with limited utility cost
relation to us: Alternative shared-bottleneck interpretation; not white-box durability

paper: SafeConstellations
authors: Utsav Maskey; Sumit Yadav; Mark Dras; Usman Naseem
problem: How to reduce over-refusal with task-specific safety geometry
method: Task-specific activation trajectories/constellations
central result: Reportedly reduces over-refusal while retaining safety
relation to us: Shows richer geometry can serve usability rather than durability

paper: Alignment-Weighted DPO
authors: Mengxuan Hu; Vivek Datla; Anoop Kumar; Zihan Guan; Sheng Li; Alfy Samuel; Daben Liu
problem: How to prevent shallow refusal in reasoning models
method: Chain-of-thought safety data and segment-weighted DPO
central result: Deeper response-level safety improves robustness
relation to us: Alternative training-signal mechanism; not weight-tamper endpoint
